In the heart of Hanoi, Vietnam's capital city, lies the Vietnam National Puppetry Theatre, a tranquil oasis nestled on bustling Truong Chinh Street. Established in 1956, this esteemed institution has been dedicated to preserving the country's rich cultural heritage, specifically the traditional puppetry art form that originated in the 11th century.

The theatre's name is a testament to the legend of Chú Tễu, a gentle and witty puppet character that embodies the aspirations of Vietnamese farmers.
